source.title: $\beta $-DARTS++: Bi-Level Regularization for Proxy-Robust Differentiable Architecture Search
source.authors: Peng Ye; Tong He; Bao-Pu Li; Tao Chen; Lei Bai; Wanli Ouyang

record.file_problem: Full paper and appendices supplied. Some tables/figures are flattened or lack recoverable per-cell associations; numerical results are recorded only where attribution is clear.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests differentiable architecture search stability, architecture transfer across datasets, and search robustness under reduced proxies. Its use of “generalization” concerns searched architectures transferring across datasets, not the claim’s train/test generalization from fitting natural labels; it does not test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own results on proxy robustness and cross-dataset architecture transfer, but no results on memorizing random labels, train/test gaps from fitting natural labels, network-width interpolation, convolution versus fully connected generalization, optimizer comparisons, batch-size effects, dropout, sharpness-gap correlations, or removal of memorized examples. Mentioned results from cited studies, including RLNAS, were not treated as this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study tests architecture-search stability, cross-dataset architecture transfer, and robustness to reduced search proxies. None measures a listed claim version. Proxy-channel changes evaluate architectures selected by search, not widening a fixed network past interpolation (V2). Architecture-parameter regularization comparisons do not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD (V4), and landscape-smoothing arguments do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness against generalization gaps (V7).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that Beta-Decay improves DARTS search stability and cross-dataset architecture transfer, and that weight flooding further improves robustness under reduced search proxies.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates regularized differentiable architecture search and proxy robustness, not the original claim’s interventions or train/test-gap measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Search outcomes vary with proxy data, channels, layers, epochs, and regularization choices; the authors report different effects across methods and proxy settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Beta-Decay improves search stability and the performance of architectures transferred across datasets. In Table 5, architectures searched on CIFAR-10 or ImageNet16-120 attain 94.36%, 73.51%, and 46.34% test accuracy on the three NAS-Bench-201 datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Regularizing activated architecture parameters can improve differentiable architecture-search stability and cross-dataset architecture transfer.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight flooding improves search performance under reduced proxies. With 20% proxy data, Table 12 reports CIFAR-100 test accuracy increasing from 70.25% without flooding to 72.98% with flooding coefficient 1.0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight flooding can improve differentiable architecture-search robustness to reduced computational proxies.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
record.problems: The evidence concerns architecture-search benchmark performance and cross-dataset transfer rather than train/test error gaps for trained networks. Many proxy results are averaged over 3 independent searches; some figures are smoothed, and flattened tables limit recovery of certain per-method/per-metric associations.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version rows apply. Proxy robustness and cross-dataset transfer findings are described under fits_no_version; cited prior work and values not clearly attributable in flattened tables were excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and its coexistence with natural-label generalization; random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error when widening networks beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Held-out performance of adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning conditions and recovery strategies.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and changes that reduce the large-batch penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness correlations with train/test gaps and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Keeping claim-version rows and verdict labels empty is appropriate. The random-label NAS result is attributed to RLNAS, not produced by this study. References to original sources do not establish tests of their claim versions.

versions.untested_parts: Whether architectures that fit random labels generalize on natural labels, including random-label held-out accuracy.
Whether widening beyond the interpolation threshold lowers test error.
Convolution versus fully connected generalization on image tasks.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization under tuning, weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Large-batch effects on train/test generalization under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Whether magnitude-aware sharpness tracks train/test generalization gaps.
Whether removing memorized training examples reduces test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
